shots.observation: Reviewed all 120 whole-scene frame thumbnails across the previous and current audit, all 120 native hand crops, all 120 native print crops, the face-candidate sheet, the actual 768p input and M01 artwork. The left dorsal hand, lower opposing thumb, wrist and original arm remain coherent; no palm reversal, extra hand or real head/face was observed. Inert printed eyes stay open and glasses remain present. This preserves the v10 small grip/fabric motion with camera push-in; it is not a large curtain-opening action. The charm is cropped by the lower image edge late in the unused tail. Assistant image-sequence review, not human continuous playback.

Reviewed all 120 whole-scene frame thumbnails, native first/last full-scene viewing copies, the sole face candidate and actual input. The candidate is tree-bark texture, not a human. The lake shore, mountains, rocks, cloud shadows and water evolve continuously without a scene reset or added person. No character print, costume or hand occurs, so artwork-specific anatomy checks do not apply. Some distant foliage remains soft; native dimensions alone are not a claim of perfect photographic texture. Assistant image-sequence review, not human continuous playback.

Reviewed corrected v2 all 120 whole-scene frames, all 120 native badge crops in eight original PNG pages, face candidates and native first-frame crop against M05 original artwork. Open eye contours, iris detail and fine round gold glasses now match the artwork and remain inert; the graphic follows the same original physical badge, its rim and chain. No new real person, human face, limb or scene discontinuity observed. Existing leg/arm motion is retained. v1 remains rejected for an incomplete replacement boundary; original and both correction versions are preserved. Assistant image-sequence acceptance, not human continuous playback or final-film approval.

Reviewed all 120 whole-scene frame thumbnails, all 120 print-region frames (native first page and native-derived viewing proxies for the remaining seven pages), face candidates, actual input and M01/original chibi artwork. No real person is present. The charm remains a rigid printed object attached to the original chain; the open eye outlines, round glasses, hair and costume remain stable with no blink or autonomous limb motion. Bag/bench/background motion remains continuous. Face candidates are charm, station fixture and bench texture. This is assistant image-sequence acceptance of this source, not final-film or human aesthetic acceptance.

Viewed all 120 whole-scene frame thumbnails through four JPEG viewing copies, all 120 tracked native sticker crops (first two PNG pages and six native-derived JPEG pages), the face-candidate sheet, native full-frame f048 and f119, the actual 768p input f000 and its sticker crop, and compared with the original chibi artwork reviewed in this session. Only the original female cyclist is present, framed below the head, in the established white/violet/gold clothing. Both legs pedal continuously; road, trees, bicycle and background remain continuous with no observed scene reset. The 49 machine cut candidates occur within this cycling motion and are not observed shot changes. The sticker stays fixed to the same frame tube, its eyes remain open and round glasses persist without blinking or autonomous movement. Face candidates include printed artwork, bike parts and background texture; none is a real human face. Native texture remains somewhat processed and wheel spokes have motion blur. Assistant image-sequence source review, not human continuous playback or final-film acceptance.

After rejecting the original iris and glasses degradation, viewed all 120 corrected whole-scene frames through four bound JPEG pages, all 120 native printed eye crops (first PNG page and seven native-derived JPEG pages), the corrected face-candidate sheet, corrected native full-frame f119, original native f000/f119, original input crop and M09 reference artwork. The M09 open violet-pink irises and thin gold round frames remain fixed across the full source, following the same sticker without blinking, facial animation or visible sliding. The local feathered eye/glasses masks avoid the visibly circular whole-face boundary that caused candidate v1 to be rejected at f000. The existing head outline, body and street motion remain present; no real person or human face appears in the scene/reflection. Candidate detections are print/clothing, trees and building texture. Native texture around the restored graphic remains processed; this is assistant source image-sequence acceptance, not human continuous playback or final-film aesthetic approval.

Actually reviewed all 120 corrected whole-scene frames and all 120 native-derived printed eye/glasses crops, corrected candidate sheet (38 entries) and native full frame 119. Compared with original M08 RGBA artwork and actual 768P input frame 0. Original source also had all 120 whole frames, all 120 print crops and all 120 crops of each attached hand viewed, plus original candidate sheet and native context. Original M08 iris and thin round gold frames restored only inside feathered lens/bridge masks; reference mask scale .39. Eyes stay OPEN, fixed to the swinging pouch with no blink or observed sliding. Continuous alternating steps start immediately, two original attached hands keep normal joints and grip, head stays outside frame, no added person observed. The original body/hair print remains softened, not claimed pixel-perfect. Nineteen cut flags resolve to walking and leaves; 112 face-candidate frames require context, reviewed examples are foliage, rocks, boots and clothing. All 120 source frames reviewed; final uses the unchanged first 96 frames/four seconds. No final-film/persona/human-playback approval.

Actually viewed all 120 whole-scene source frames through four bound JPEG contact pages, all 120 native-derived plush face crops and all 120 native-derived badge crops through eight JPEG pages each, the 30-example face candidate sheet and native full frames 0 and 119. Compared with actual 768P input frames 0, 96 and 119 and original M04 plush/M05 badge artwork read in this session. Both merchandise faces retain open violet-pink eyes and round gold glasses, fixed to their surfaces, with no blink or autonomous toy motion. The maple leaf falls across the plush eye then clears it; this is physical occlusion already present in the actual input, not a closed-eye expression. Badge colors are paler and detail softer than the master, but its open eye shape, irises and round frames remain readable and stable; no repair selected. Empty woodland, bag and bench remain continuous throughout the slow push-in; no real person, human face, added hand or observed shot cut. Candidate examples are merchandise, bag fittings and woodland texture. Source-image sequence acceptance only, not human continuous playback or formal final-film/persona approval.

Actually viewed every one of 120 corrected whole-scene source frames through four bound JPEG pages, all 120 native-derived eye/glasses crops through eight JPEG pages, the 14-example corrected face candidate sheet and corrected native context frame 119. Compared original M09 RGBA artwork, actual 768P input first frame and four first-frame registration candidates before adopting candidate 02 parameters. Original whole scene and wide attached-hand crops were separately reviewed across all 120 frames. Restored open pink/violet star irises and thin gold round glasses remain attached to the same bottle sticker without autonomous expression, visible slip or blinking. Original and corrected eyes were OPEN; original rejection concerned lost iris/glasses detail. One original hand rests palm-down on the railing with gentle finger motion, connected to the same feminine sleeved forearm. No added hand/person, human head/face, scene reset or impossible wrist observed. River, reflection, railing and bottle motion stay continuous. Native-derived candidate examples are distant bank/foliage, railing and bottle edges, not real people. Only eye/glasses texture restored; hair and body print remain softer, and the complete frame was re-encoded at CRF16. All 120 frames reviewed though only original 3 seconds / 72 native frames enter the film. Assistant image-sequence review, not human continuous playback or final-film approval. Supplemental actual review: all 137 detector boxes across 109 frames were viewed through nine native-derived JPEG contact pages, retaining all 137 native PNGs separately. They show bank roots/rocks/foliage, slanting railing, existing sleeve and bottle edges. No observed real face or added person. Detector misses remain possible; this supplements the complete whole-scene review.

Actually viewed all 120 whole-scene source frames through four bound JPEG pages, all 120 native-derived crops of each original hand through sixteen JPEG contact pages, all 285 detector boxes across all 120 candidate frames through eighteen native-derived JPEG contact pages, the original 25-example candidate sheet, native whole frame 119 and two wider native context crops from frame 108. Compared actual 768P input first frame and original P03 back-view artwork. The same one illustrated woman remains strictly back-facing, with stable silver hair, beret, blue butterfly ornament, feminine white/deep violet/gold dress, white legwear and purple boots. Both original resting hands stay attached to the correct sleeved forearms on the railing; no extra limb, palm reversal or changing wrist anatomy observed. Fingers overlap in the resting side view; not a claim of independently counted visible fingers in every frame. Water ripples, small hair and ribbon movements and fixed camera remain continuous. No head turn, eye/face reveal, added person, real face, reflection of people or scene cut observed. Detector boxes show trees, distant building/roof textures, stone pavement and a rusty railing junction; the two small distant clusters and right-edge brown/white cluster were checked in wider frame-108 context. No visible character eyes in this back view; no eye restoration needed. Original native source accepted, all original five seconds / 120 native frames retained. Assistant image-sequence review, not human continuous playback or formal film approval.
